newsitem.title: CHINA: China media says no deaths in Beijing blast.
newsitem.headline: China media says no deaths in Beijing blast.

text.p: An explosion that ripped through a Beijing bus as it trundled through a busy shopping district caused no deaths but injured more than 10 passengers, Chinese police and state media said on Saturday.
Chinese sources said at least two people were killed when a bomb detonated aboard the city bus in the capital's bustling western Xidan district on Friday evening.
The official Beijing Daily and police confirmed the blast took place, but gave no details.
"Yesterday evening at about 7.00 pm (1100 GMT), an explosion occurred on a city Number 22 bus at the Xidan Market stop," the Beijing Daily said in a brief front-page report.
"More than 10 passengers were hurt, none was killed," the newspaper said.
None of the people hurt in the blast had life-threatening injuries, a Beijing police spokeswoman said.
Workers at an emergency centre near the bustling commercial area, where many shops stay open until late evening, said they had sent about 30 people to nearby hospitals for treatment.
One bystander said he saw the explosion blow the windows out of the back of the articulated city bus and reported seeing about nine people seriously hurt.
"The bomb blast was not very loud, but it blew out the back window and everybody ran," he said.
"There was a great flame and a 'boom' sound and then people jumped out of the bus," said a young man who was working nearby.

By Saturday morning all appeared normal in Xidan district, where shoppers crowded department stores along the main thoroughfare which had been swept clean of glass shards that littered the road after the blast.
Local shopkeepers working just metres from the scene of the blast appeared unconcerned by the nearby drama.
"Don't foreign countries also have this kind of incident, with bombs far more serious than this one?" said a worker in a Xidan shoe shop.
Police officials said they had yet to establish what had caused the explosion.
"We are currently investigating... it is not clear," said the Beijing police spokeswoman.
The Beijing bus blast follows a string of attacks by Moslem separatists in the restive far-western region of Xinjiang.

Three bombs planted on buses blew up within minutes of each other on February 25 in the regional capital of Urumqi in an attack apparently coordinated to coincide with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Nine people were killed and 74 wounded.
